composition_rules.document_shape: setup-format r13 §2.11: the primary setup holds modifiers: {setupId, role}[] (DSK)
primary_owns: targeting (UNIT/TILE pipe, or none = no pipe)
composition_rules.scaler: runs before resolve, adjusts the primary's declared numeric_inputs, never targets; a scaler's targeting fields are ignored with modifierFieldIgnored
composition_rules.rider: runs after resolve. Riders keep their own targeting knobs, re-anchored: their origin is the primary's resolved target(s), not the caster (e.g. Heavenly Sword's push rider aims from the hit unit). Engine Architect 2026-11-09

ruling.note: ability = one primary behaviour + ordered modifiers[] {setupId, role: scaler|rider} (document_shape); the ability document shape is DSK's

composition_rules.targeting_none: No third pipe. An ability may have targeting: none ('no pipe'): CHOOSE_ACTION goes straight to resolve, the resolve context gets the caster only, and any effect needing a location uses the caster's cell. Self-target is the UNIT pipe with the caster. Engine Architect 2026-11-09
composition_rules.ability_field: ability_field tags (targeting | group | effect | cost) name the ability field a primary's knob feeds. On a rider, targeting knobs stay live but are re-anchored to the primary's resolved target(s); on a scaler they are ignored (modifierFieldIgnored).
composition_rules.mapping_note: compositions[].modifiers[].behaviourId is a catalogue-level mapping (which behaviour a card's modifier is), not the document field; documents use {setupId, role} (DSK L40).

rulings.note: pattern and max_step don't conflict. pattern sets the shape and reach for each unit; the default stays orthogonal-1, from BTF's piece tables and towerChess moveSquares/legalSteps. max_step is only a ceiling on the whole project (how-to-play: 'No step is longer than two tiles'). It never makes a step longer than the pattern allows. If a pattern's reach is longer than max_step, the extra tiles are clamped and the validator gives a stepClamped warning; the file keeps the value. So with the defaults (orthogonal-1 under max_step 2), a unit moves 1 tile. A 2-tile mover picks orthogonal-2 or king-2.

Withdrawn in catalogue rev 29 (option (a)): S1 follows the BTF default. Any living body stops a long step (towerChess.ts empty() :399-407, ray :424). No picker. The earlier own-team pass-through ruling is withdrawn.

invariants: pattern and max_step don't conflict: pattern sets the shape and reach for each unit; max_step is only a project ceiling (how-to-play: 'No step is longer than two tiles') and never makes a step longer than the pattern allows. If a pattern's reach is longer than max_step, extra tiles are clamped (validator warning stepClamped; the file keeps the value). With the defaults (orthogonal-1 under max_step 2), a unit moves 1 tile. A 2-tile mover picks orthogonal-2 or king-2. (EA 2026-11-17, Phase 1 freeze, recut fcb61019.)

orthogonal-2 moves straight only, with no turn (one ray along N, E, S or W; BTF isCleric, towerChess.ts:465-470). Each ray stops at walls (seamBlocks, :424 / towerTerrain.ts:1251), at blocked tiles, and at occupied tiles. v1: any living body stops the ray and cannot be landed on (empty() :399-407; bodies_block_long_step default true; how-to-play.md:22). EA's own-team pass-through ruling was withdrawn in rev 29 (option (a); no picker; gaps §35).

behaviours.name: Barrier Line on a Tile Seam (earth) and Cage
behaviours.summary: A wall sits on the edge between two tiles, not on a tile. A seam blocks only the side it sits on. It blocks steps for both sides and soaks enemy shots that would cross it; your own shots pass. Variants grow one wall facing an enemy, scatter walls round enemies, or box an enemy in on three sides. It joins a project's closure only through a setup (the ordinary rule); a map's edges alone never pull it in, and without it authored walls are indestructible.

invariants: A seam blocks only the side it sits on. behaviours.name: Holy Sword Lifecycle (spawn -> curve leap -> become unit, or fade)
behaviours.summary: A summoned sword fades in on its tile (lost if a body is standing there when the fade ends). Fresh, it can leap once: it flies on a curved arc that bows away from the target and lands on the nearest open tile beside any enemy, hitting for 2. After landing it is an ordinary 1-health piece with attack 1 that you control (one king step, bite 1). It gains +1/+1 if it kills a neutral. It never respawns, isn't counted for the clock, and its presence gives Lucifer his second action.

presets.cards: Renegade, Morning Star, Pride in Numbers swords
presets.source: /workspace/g-tile-engine/src/chess/game/towerLucifer.ts bladeLanding(), bladeTargets(), tapFreshBlade(), launchBlade(), tick loop over flies, blockLanding(), launchDemonBlade(); towerLuciferGuest.ts sendGuestBlade(); towerTerrain.ts seamBlocks()
notes: Candidates: the 8 tiles around the target (neighbors(): dc -1..1, then dr -1..1, on the board). A tile counts if it is empty (the sword itself ignored) and seamBlocks(tile, target) is false. seamBlocks only checks orthogonal neighbours, so a diagonal tile is never walled off. (towerLucifer.ts bladeLanding, neighbors; towerTerrain.ts seamBlocks)

Order (player and online-guest swords): the candidate with the smallest Manhattan distance from the sword wins. Ties go to the first in neighbors() order, because the comparison is strict '<'. (bladeLanding)

Order (demon AI swords): blockLanding() sorts candidates: first the tile one step from the target toward the AI's Lucifer, then tiles nearer Lucifer than the target is, then nearest Lucifer. The AI also prefers swords not standing in the gap between Lucifer and the target, then the sword nearest the landing tile. (blockLanding, launchDemonBlade)

Flask fallback: if no candidate is free and the target is soul-linked to a flask (contestLinked), the first neighbour holding a flask (contestBlocks) with no seam to the target is used. (bladeLanding)

Path: nothing on the way is checked. The sword flies a curved hop that bends away from the target (bladeFlightPoint) over bodies and earth lines. That bending is the 'swerve'; it's cosmetic, and only the landing tile matters.

No reachable tile: the foe isn't a target. bladeTargets() leaves it out, tapFreshBlade() returns false, no action is spent, the sword stays fresh, and there is nothing to refund because the summon card was already paid. The AI skips that foe and tries the next; if none works, no sword launches (launchDemonBlade returns null). The guest call returns false.
Landing tile taken by the time of the hit: the sword stays where it was, but the hit still lands for BLADE_AD. Afterwards its attack drops to BLADE_AD_AFTER. (towerLucifer.ts flies tick)
Cost: a player sword spends one action (chess.left, or focusLeft under a focus card). Guest and AI launches don't touch the action count. (tapFreshBlade, sendGuestBlade)

knobs.description: The rule (r27, M2; EA G2b item 10 word for word): `pixel_scale` absent or `null` = today's `k` rule; `"match-sprite"` = the anchor unit's sprite pixel size; a JSON integer 1–6 = that pixel size; the strings `"1"`–`"6"` are read as aliases of the integers and rewritten to integers on edit (M6); anything else (0, 7, 2.5, other strings) warns once (`outOfRange` for a number, the unknown-option warning for a string, per M5) and plays as the `k` rule. Absent/`null` and `"match-sprite"` are distinct. Rule N (the editor writes "match-sprite" into new documents, CEO Q2) is an editor write, not the catalogue default. A wrong JSON type (true, an object, an array) stays H2 invalidValue.

knobs.description: Rev 23 (Effects v2, DSK L46-L48): up to 12 steps; four new kinds (dim, stamp, particles, flash); timing (start_mode, start_at_ms, hold_ms, fade_out_ms); Feel tricks (circle flash, rings, blank, smear, shine) and step-33 sync, depth, light and colour fields. Every new field is optional: absent means exactly today's play, so a stored step may leave any item field out and it reads as that field's default (item_absent_reads_default; setup-format §2.10.1 'Old effects don't move', §12.5 L46 item 7). The 10 btf-* presets keep their stored steps unchanged. Fields apply only to the kinds their item_cites name; elsewhere they are kept and ignored. Rev 24 (DSK L49): dim_lights on dim steps, picker half|dark, default half. Old stored steps leave it out and it reads as half. On any other kind it is kept and ignored silently. Rev 25 (L50, L52): part tags a step to one of the effect's parts (editor only); ride lets a particles, stamp or circle-flash step follow a travel step's path (IDEA, RISKY). Both are optional with no default: absent means untagged / its own anchor, so old stored steps and the catalogue default step leave them out.

item_cites.ride: /workspace/tileengine/handoff/change-notices/CN-026-effect-step-ride.md (sha256 60e08878) Keys and rules 1-9 (L52; IDEA, RISKY per the EA; CN-026 ACCEPTED, DSK 11:59; rev 26 re-checked every rule against CN-026 sha256 60e08878: rules 1, 1b, 2, 3, 4, 4b, 5-9 all match this field; d9037136 was the reviewed PROPOSED draft named by the staged entry (no copy on disk; the nearest backup is r2 PROPOSED 49e1a91b), so nothing differs); staged entry _src/staging/L52-ride.json (sha256 dff693a6). Pick another step in this effect for this one to ride along. Particles, stamps and flashes then follow that step's travel path instead of sitting at their own anchor. Rules: (1) Optional; absent means none. A null or other non-string value is H2 invalidValue. (2) One hop only: a rider follows the named step's own path and never that step's ride. (3) If the named step is missing, disabled or dropped by Fit, the rider plays at its own anchor and raises an unknownRef warning (the runtime can't tell a dropped id from a missing one; CN-026 rule 5). (4) Flatten removes a ride whose named step isn't on the rider's own side. (5) A lit stamp or particles rider (light_mode set) carries its light along the path; light is not a step kind. (6) A flash with flash_shape "screen" doesn't move when riding, and no note is raised. (7) A ride on a step kind that can't ride (anything other than particles, stamp and flash) is ignored but kept, never stripped. A rider takes the path and timing of a travel step (straight, swerve, bounce, orbit) among the first 12 (rule 1). An empty string, an unknown id, its own id, a non-travel, disabled or past-12 step is unknownRef, kept, and the rider plays at its anchor (rule 3). A disabled rider plays nothing with no note (4b). Flatten re-points a ride to the moved step's fresh id (rule 6). Clearing writes absent, never "" or null (rule 8). Absent hashes as today; a present ride is a look change (rule 9)

ui_derived.label: Speed
ui_derived.rule: UI-only multiplier: multiplies every steps[].seconds by the factor and writes those values (each clamped to 0.15-3). The factor itself is never stored. Rev 23: it also scales start_at_ms, hold_ms, fade_out_ms, particle_life_ms and flash_ms (§2.10.1.3 rule 3a) and blank_ms, shine_ms and shine_loop_rest_ms (§2.10.2.4, §2.10.2.8), each clamped to its range. It never scales hit_stop_ms.

ui_derived.label: Count
ui_derived.rule: Edits row_count or orbit_count on the first step whose kind is row or orbit; disabled with a hint when there is none. Rev 23: it also scales particle_count on the particles steps, capped at 48 (§2.10.1.3 rule 3a).

ui_derived.label: Dim the stage
ui_derived.rule: Maps to steps.enabled of the dim steps. Turning it on with no dim step inserts one at its defaults with start_mode at-time (§2.10.1.3 rule 3a, L46).

ui_derived.label: Flash
ui_derived.rule: Maps to steps.enabled of the flash steps whose flash_strength is above 0 (§2.10.1.3 rule 3a, L46).

ui_derived.label: Impact flash
ui_derived.rule: On when the effect has an enabled at-hit white circle flash with offset 0 followed in list order by an at-hit black circle flash; turning it on writes the two §2.10.2.2 steps (and pins connect_step first, §2.10.2.1); off sets enabled false on that pair (L47).

ui_derived.label: Shockwave
ui_derived.rule: On when the effect has an enabled at-hit ring-only flash step (flash_strength 0) on ground; off sets enabled false (§2.10.2.3, L47).

ui_derived.label: Blank punch
ui_derived.rule: On when any enabled step has blank_ms above 0; off writes 0 or enabled false (§2.10.2.12, L47).

ui_derived.label: Hit-stop
ui_derived.rule: On when hit_stop_ms is above 0; the toggle writes 50, off writes 0 (§2.10.2.5, §2.10.2.12, L47).

ui_derived.label: Smear
ui_derived.rule: On when smear_ms is above 0; the toggle writes 40, off writes 0 (§2.10.2.6, L47).

ui_derived.label: Hit-white
ui_derived.rule: On when hit_white_ms is above 0; the toggle writes 40, off writes 0 (§2.10.2.7, L47).

ui_derived.label: Shine
ui_derived.rule: On when shine_ms is above 0; the toggle writes 320, off writes 0 (§2.10.2.8, L47).

behaviours.name: Terrain (what each tile id means)
behaviours.summary: The single home for tile meanings: for each logic tile id, whether units can stand, land or spawn there, whether landing kills, whether a push can enter, and whether it slows or trips. Edge walls (earth lines) are not tiles in the code: they sit on a tile's n/e/s/w edge and live in Barrier Line. Walls on tile edges (the map's logic.edges) always block movement and adjacency across that edge: that is core grid behaviour with no knob. The two wall knobs only decide whether walls also block line of sight and shots.

knobs.description: Built-ins water, lava and wall-block are CONFIRMED engine defaults (Engine Architect 2026-11-09, L27) and the defaultTileType targets of the procedural recipes (project-format r13 section 6.2.2 / 6.4): water@2 and murk@1 give water, lava@2 gives lava, wall gives wall-block, ice@1 gives floor in v1 (slippery ice is a future tile type), the rest give floor. buildable (item field, rev 15, PROPOSED, modes: td; v1: false): whether a structure may be placed on the tile. False on every built-in, floor included: grid tactics has no building and BTF never places structures, so false keeps tactics unchanged; a TD project sets it on its own tile types (Engine Architect / Modes Designer MODES-v2 §3, DSK L41). An added item field, so stored lists are not flagged. Rev 23 (DSK L45): built-ins path and dirt (walkable land, like floor, not buildable); 15 reserved items. wall-block stays the only catalogue spelling; wall_block is a reader alias in the format only (setup-format §2.9.3 rule 7). Existing answers drift by §2.9.3 rules 4 and 6 (appended to the effective value, nothing written).

behaviours.summary: Held tools swing at the faced cell: a binding table maps a held item's tag and a motion to what it may hit and the rules action it fires (mine, plough, chop, hit), and prop rows make map objects finish after a number of hits and drop a loot table. knobs.label: Swing bindings (first match wins)
knobs.default_source: /workspace/tileengine/handoff/change-notices/CN-027-tool-swing-format.md (sha256 78f9d7b0, ACCEPTED) rules 18-23 (L53; line 44-62): rows {id, label, item_tag, motion, target_tags, action}; first match in stored order; the default = the CN's four item-first preset rows (ordinary default items, not reserved_ids). IDEA until TSa builds the rules slice
knobs.description: The binding table: the rules take the held item's tags and the target's tags and use the FIRST row whose item_tag is one of the item's tags and whose target_tags is empty or shares a tag. No specificity scoring; the editor adds new maker rows above the preset rows. A row fully covered by an earlier one (same item_tag, earlier target_tags [] or a superset) warns bindingShadowed (EA ruling g); both are kept. No matching row: if the item has any row its first row's motion plays with no action (a prop gets the wrong-tool tink); else nothing plays. The four default rows are frozen ids, deletable and reorderable (no reservedMissing). tool and weapon get no default row.

knobs.label: Prop rows (map objects a swing can finish)
knobs.default_source: /workspace/tileengine/handoff/change-notices/CN-027-tool-swing-format.md (sha256 78f9d7b0, ACCEPTED) rules 24-28 (L53; lines 65-70-78): rows {id, label, tags, hits_to_finish, reacts_to?, yields}; no asset field (EA ruling d); a map placement becomes a prop by naming a row id in objects[].prop (project-format §6.4; not CoreMapObject). Default [] = no map object is a prop (today). IDEA until TSa
knobs.description: A prop row is found from the map placement (objects[].prop names a row id), never from the art, so a repaint keeps it a prop. Hits to finish, progress, reacts-to and yields live only here and in rules state (propHit); progress is never written into the map. A prop that names no row warns unknownRef and the object plays as today. Many placements may share a row. Wrong JS types and bad id/label are H2 (rule 28).

invariants: Props are never units: a prop stays a TILE occupant with no unit id, side or HP, is never UNIT-targetable and never in loadouts or pools; 'unit' in props[].tags warns outOfRange and is ignored (CN-027 rule 24 and Guards).
Nothing new on CoreMapObject: hits, progress, reacts-to and yields live on the props row and in rules state; the only new map key is objects[].prop (CN-027 rules 25-27).

ideas.summary: The default element-reaction table the Effect Designer offers when reactions are switched on: mixing two ramps suggests a ready-made look. Editor suggestions only; never read at match time.
ideas.absent_means: reactions off (no suggestions); this table is only the content offered when the maker turns them on
ideas.source: /workspace/tileengine/handoff/change-notices/CN-022-project-effect-shelf-house.md (sha256 ab5232ea) 'Reaction table'; /workspace/share/effect-designer/scope.md (r4 APPROVED + §13 r5, sha256 2b81170c) §7 CN-022, §10 B-5 (line 171), §12 Q6 (a) / Q7 (a), §13 (line 256); /workspace/share/effect-designer/bold-inputs-librarian-modes.md (sha256 08f08ea2)
constraints: Shape per CN-022: [{a: rampKey, b: rampKey, effect: effectId}]. The catalogue adds id, label, suggests, status, seeds and notes for the CEO; the editor writes only a, b and effect.

a and b are palette ramp keys (the six terrain keys plus fire, frost, holy, venom). DSK rule (2026-11-16): pairs are unordered and a == b is allowed (fire + fire); if both orders are stored, the first in stored order wins and the other gets an info note; the table is suggestions only. The catalogue table itself stores each pair once.
effect names a look. None of these looks exists yet, so each is a placeholder id (effect_placeholder true); CN-022 makes a dangling effect ref info only.
BTF has no element-reaction rules, only stacking or swapping arms. Every pair is seeded from those arms; fire + frost has no BTF arm and is kept only as the scope's example.
No match-time reactions (CEO Q7 (a)); a fused look in play is the B-8 host swap of a ready-made look (CEO Q6 (a)).
Seed src paths are relative to /workspace/g-tile-engine/src (the canonical code); each was re-read for this pass.
Store name: CN-022 stores the table as project-root effectReactions; the scope (§7) calls it reactions. The catalogue follows CN-022.
